## Increment: order-independent suffix-first exclusion
Let T(S) be the exact set of labels whose germ set intersects S. For any linear partition L=(L+,L-), T((A union X) intersect L+) = T(A intersect L+) union T(X intersect L+), and likewise for L-. Proof: distributivity of intersection over union followed by the exact label-union identity of R296. This factorization is valid for each particular declared split; no replacement of full germs by unconditioned label marginals is made. At depth five, if a branch contains 31 labels, R247's saturated necessary-wall rule restricts the first suffix split to the 47 frozen wall normals. Each child has depth four and capacity 15. Thus if every wall has a child with >15 labels, the branch is impossible. A root word with such a branch is excluded independently of existence of its quadratic separator. This reorders two necessary conditions without needing to solve its coefficient algebra. Unsaturated branches and branches with at least one permitted first split remain unknown under this check. Original germ masks and signed endpoint associations retained. No claim that this test is sufficient or that the 47-wall rule applies to unsaturated branches.
